name.en: Kisan Vikas Patra (KVP) — Post Office Savings Certificate

authority: Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance / India Post

description.en: Kisan Vikas Patra (KVP) is a savings certificate scheme offered by India Post under the Government of India's Small Savings Schemes. KVP doubles the invested amount in approximately 115 months (9 years and 7 months) at the prevailing interest rate. It can be purchased from any post office or designated nationalized banks. KVP is available in denominations of Rs. 1,000, Rs. 5,000, Rs. 10,000, and Rs. 50,000 with no maximum investment limit. The certificates are transferable between persons and pledgeable as collateral for loans. KVP is governed by the Kisan Vikas Patra Rules 2014 under the Government Savings Certificates Act 1959.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: Indian residents above 18 years of age
verifiedConditions.claim: KVP can be purchased by any adult Indian citizen who is a resident of India. Joint accounts (up to 3 adults) are permitted. A guardian may purchase KVP on behalf of a minor or a person of unsound mind.

The minimum investment amount for KVP is Rs. 1,000 and thereafter in multiples of Rs. 100. There is no maximum limit on investment. However, for purchases of Rs. 50,000 or above, PAN is mandatory, and for purchases of Rs. 10 lakh or above, income proof is required.

unverifiedEligibility: Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) and Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs) are not eligible to purchase KVP.
Trusts are not eligible to purchase KVP.
A minor who has attained the age of 10 years may purchase KVP in their own name with certain conditions.

requirements.claim: Duly filled KVP application form available at any post office or designated bank branch. The form requires details of the applicant, nominee, amount of investment, and denomination of certificates required.
Valid identity proof — Aadhaar card, voter ID, passport, or driving licence. KYC documents are mandatory under Prevention of Money Laundering Act requirements for all small savings scheme purchases.
Valid address proof — Aadhaar card, passport, utility bill (not older than 3 months), or bank passbook with address. Required as part of KYC compliance for purchase of KVP certificates.
PAN card or Form 60 declaration is mandatory for single or aggregate purchases of Rs. 50,000 or above in a financial year, as required under Income Tax Act provisions for small savings schemes.

For investments of Rs. 10 lakh and above, proof of source of income is mandatory. Acceptable documents include salary slips, bank statements, IT return acknowledgement, or an affidavit declaring the source of funds.
Two recent passport-sized photographs of each applicant (and guardian, if applicable) for KYC records. Joint applicants must each provide photographs.

processInformation.claim: Visit any post office (Head Post Office, Sub Post Office, or Branch Post Office) or designated nationalized bank branch. Obtain the KVP application form and fill in the required details including name, address, nominee details, and investment amount.

Submit the completed application form along with KYC documents (identity proof, address proof, photographs), PAN card (if amount is Rs. 50,000 or above), and income proof (if amount is Rs. 10 lakh or above). Make payment by cash (up to Rs. 50,000), cheque, or demand draft.

The post office issues the KVP certificate on the spot for cash payments, or within 1-3 days for cheque/DD payments (after clearing). The certificate bears the purchaser's name, denomination, date of purchase, and maturity date. A passbook-style KVP account is maintained.

At maturity (approximately 115 months at current rates), present the KVP certificate at any post office along with identity proof for encashment. The maturity value (double the invested amount) is paid. Premature encashment is permitted after 30 months (2.5 years) from the date of purchase, subject to applicable interest rate and terms.

output.claim: A Kisan Vikas Patra certificate is issued in the name of the purchaser (or joint holders) indicating the denomination, date of purchase, and maturity date. The certificate doubles the invested amount at maturity (approximately 115 months at the prevailing interest rate of 7.5% compounded annually). KVP certificates are transferable to another person and can be pledged as security for obtaining loans from banks.

fees.claim: There is no additional fee or commission charged for purchasing KVP certificates. The entire amount paid goes towards the investment. The minimum purchase amount is Rs. 1,000 with no maximum limit. Certificates are available in denominations of Rs. 1,000, Rs. 5,000, Rs. 10,000, and Rs. 50,000.

fees.applicability: Fee for transfer of KVP certificate from one person to another or between post offices
fees.claim: A nominal fee of approximately Rs. 50 may be charged for transfer of KVP certificates from one person to another, or for transfer between post offices. Transfer requires Form SF-5 and consent of both transferor and transferee. Transfer is permitted on grounds such as sale, gift, court order, or succession.

processingTime.applicability: KVP certificate issuance from application to receipt
processingTime.claim: KVP certificates are issued on the same day for cash purchases (counter issuance). For purchases by cheque or demand draft, the certificate is issued within 1-3 working days after cheque clearing. The maturity period is approximately 115 months (9 years and 7 months) at the current interest rate of 7.5% compounded annually.

Available in denominations of Rs. 1,000, Rs. 5,000, Rs. 10,000 and Rs. 50,000. Maturity period approximately 115 months at current interest rate. Transferable and pledgeable. KYC mandatory. claimsSupported: KVP doubles investment in approximately 115 months.
Minimum investment Rs. 1,000, no maximum limit.
KYC and PAN required as per applicable thresholds.
Available at all post offices and designated banks.
sources.uncertainty: Interest rate is revised quarterly by the government and the maturity period adjusts accordingly.

sources.title: National Savings Institute — Small Savings Schemes Including KVP

sources.evidenceExcerpt: KVP is governed by Kisan Vikas Patra Rules 2014 under the Government Savings Certificates Act 1959. Interest rate for KVP is 7.5% compounded annually (as notified for the current quarter). The maturity amount is double the face value. Source of income declaration mandatory for purchases of Rs. 10 lakh and above. NRIs and HUFs are not eligible.
claimsSupported: KVP interest rate is 7.5% compounded annually (current quarter).
Governed by KVP Rules 2014 under Government Savings Certificates Act 1959.
Income proof required for Rs. 10 lakh and above investments.
NRIs and HUFs are not eligible to purchase KVP.
sources.uncertainty: Interest rates are subject to quarterly revision by the Ministry of Finance based on government securities yields.

limitations: KVP interest rate is revised every quarter by the Central Government and the maturity period changes accordingly. The current rate of 7.5% and 115-month maturity are indicative.
Interest earned on KVP is fully taxable under the Income Tax Act. There is no Section 80C deduction for KVP investment.
This record covers standard KVP purchase. Premature encashment terms, transfer procedures, and duplicate certificate issuance are summarized but not covered in full detail.
NRIs, HUFs, and trusts are not eligible. This record does not cover alternative small savings instruments.
Some designated bank branches may not offer KVP. Availability at banks should be confirmed.
The record does not cover the process for pledging KVP as loan collateral with banks.

review.reviewReason: Core scheme structure is stable under KVP Rules 2014 but quarterly interest rate revisions affect maturity period and returns.
nextReviewTrigger: Quarterly revision of KVP interest rate by Ministry of Finance.
Changes to KVP Rules 2014 or Government Savings Certificates Act 1959.
Changes to KYC or PAN thresholds for small savings schemes.
Changes to premature encashment terms or lock-in period.
Introduction of digital/online KVP purchase through India Post Payments Bank or DOP internet banking.
